overview: This 228-page file traces Japanese fisheries and whaling from the late 1930s into World War II. It combines consular surveys, translated fisheries-school and research regulations, commercial reports, vessel lists, and intelligence correspondence. Later documents examine Japanese fishing across the Pacific and beyond, allegations of espionage and illegal fishing, and proposals to disrupt northern fisheries during wartime.
interest: Its translated training regulations and vessel records sit alongside intelligence claims, showing how fisheries became a wartime concern.
